posts.title: Why we’re watching these climate tech companies
posts.summary: This week, we released our 2026 version of our Climate Tech Companies to Watch list. It’s an annual project that the MIT Technology Review team puts together. Our goal is to highlight some of the promising, interesting advances and firms we think are worth paying attention to in the world of climate and energy technology. …
bullets: China maintains a dominant position in global energy technology, exemplified by Envision Energy, which has deployed over 100 gigawatts of wind power and 50 gigawatt-hours of battery storage.
Chinese battery manufacturers are aggressively pursuing solid-state and semi-solid-state technologies to improve safety and energy density over standard lithium-ion cells.
WeLion New Energy has reported lab results achieving 824 watt-hours per kilogram, representing a potential threefold increase in energy density compared to current industry standards.

								By: Don Ong
								
							
For most of the semiconductor industry’s history, value was captured in fairly predictable places.
Smaller transistors, better processing nodes, and higher-performance chips.
But the industry is going into a new era.

Today, some of the most important breakthroughs are happening outside the transistor itself: in advanced packaging, in AI infrastructure, in system integration, in software, data, and platform ecosystems.

posts.title: Nio completes nearly 1.2 million battery swaps over 7-day holiday, sets daily record twice
posts.summary:
Nio's 4,168 battery swap stations completed 1,192,221 swaps from October 1 to 7, with the daily average rising 22% year-on-year.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Nio completed 1,192,221 battery swaps during the 7-day National Day holiday, with daily averages rising 22% year-on-year.
The company set two daily swap records during the period, peaking at 183,664 swaps on October 5.
Highway infrastructure proved critical, with 1,073 swap stations supplying over 24.83 million kWh of electricity and saving users over 309,000 hours of wait time.

posts.title: Li Auto to launch 2026 Li i6 on October 28, deliveries to start in early November
posts.summary:
Li Auto will begin displaying the 2026 Li i6 at 485 stores in China on October 11, with the model set to appear at the Paris Motor Show on October 12.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Li Auto will officially launch the 2026 Li i6 on October 28, with deliveries scheduled to commence in early November.
The new model will feature in-house developed 5C battery technology and Mach driver-assistance chips, reflecting the company's vertical integration strategy.
The vehicle will debut internationally at the Paris Motor Show under the 'Li 6' branding, marking a significant step in the company's global expansion.
